plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do. This ensures you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (maximizing profit) and never overpay (never lose money) when you do win. Since payment equals the second-highest bid, not my own bid, there's no benefit to shading below value. I'll bid exactly my value of $31.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because your payment depends only on the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so there's no incentive to shade your bid. Bidding truthfully maximizes expected profit: if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (which is what I'd pay regardless of my exact bid above that), and bidding my true value ensures I only win when my value exceeds the price, guaranteeing non-negative profit whenever I win.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (I pay the second-highest bid if I win). In such auctions, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy — it guarantees I never overpay and always capture positive profit when I have the highest value, since my payment only depends on others' bids, not mine. Bidding higher risks losses if I win; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With a value of $40, I will bid exactly $40 to maximize expected profit.
